claims.text: A hybrid ab initio and machine-learning framework incorporating explicit defect and oxygen scattering will predict the conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen within ±10% of experiment across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr has inherent chemical disorder.
The modeled specimen contains a controlled 1 wt.% oxygen impurity.
The modeled specimen contains a distribution of intrinsic defects.
Defect-inclusive DFT supercells can represent realistic defect and oxygen configurations in this alloy.
An active-learning loop will refine the training set by selecting undersampled defect configurations.
Defect scattering dominates conductivity behavior in the 0–200 K regime.
Phonon scattering is significant in the 300–1200 K regime.
Defect and oxygen scattering are significant in the 300–1200 K regime.
Local defect configurations alter electron-scattering pathways in disordered HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen-induced impurity states alter electron-scattering pathways in disordered HfNbTaTiZr.
Defect-inclusive DFT calculations provide scattering parameters for configurations containing explicit defects and oxygen impurities.
The ML model can learn a nonlinear relationship among scattering parameters, defect density, oxygen incorporation, temperature, and conductivity.
Including defects and oxygen explicitly will improve accuracy relative to perfect-crystal analytical approaches.
Conventional analytical models assume defect-free, perfect crystals.
Conventional analytical models have significant inaccuracies when oxygen impurities and defects are present.
The proposed model is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Reliability may diminish outside the specified composition and temperature ranges because dominant scattering mechanisms may change.
A conductivity prediction at 350 K that differs from an independent four-probe measurement by more than 10% will falsify the hypothesis.
